commits.author: penfever
commits.message:
Sort installed distributions without comparing None to a string (#11219)

Canonical verification identity sorts `(name, version)` pairs from the
installed distributions. An editable or partly removed install reports a
missing name or version, and sorting a mixture of `None` and `str`
raises `TypeError: '<' not supported between instances of 'NoneType' and
'str'`.

That failure is unrelated to the source being verified: it aborts every
step that computes a verification identity, which is why task-curation
pipeline tests on `main` fail with `RuntimeError: 1 step(s) failed`.

Both fields are now normalized before sorting, so a missing name or
version sorts as an empty string. Reproduced on `origin/main` (the file
is unchanged there); with this patch
`experiments/post_training/task_curation/tests/test_pipeline.py` goes
from 55 failing to 41 passing.

Co-authored-by: Ben Feuer <benfeuer@Bens-MacBook-Pro.local>

Gate best-checkpoint selection on preservation metrics (#10651)

Select the best checkpoint using a configured score in [0, 1], with
larger values preferred. Optional preservation gates limit absolute
drops from step-zero metric values. Delay trained-checkpoint selection
until a configured fraction of training has elapsed; retain the initial
model as a candidate and reload the original preservation baseline on

mappings.

retain the existing selection metric and impose no preservation gates.

commits.message:
[agents] Add a skill for auditing eval and reward graders (#10422)

Add audit-grader, a skill for measuring how often a grader contradicts
its task text before its scores are trusted. It covers programmatic
checkers, LLM judges, and RL reward functions, and estimates a grader's
error rate with a blinded review of frozen samples by two reviewers. The
workflow catalog lists it, as #10462 asked.

The worked example is the #10060 audit of Marin's 58 IFBench checkers.
That audit found 43 checker findings, 9 of which depend on an
interpretation decision. On held-out responses, Marin's checkers under
strict grading contradicted the consensus of two Claude Opus 5.5
reviewers on an estimated 6.1% of constraint verdicts (95% CI 3.9 to
10.1). The audit's validated checkers with IFBench's official readings
(fixes only) contradicted it on 3.2% (1.0 to 7.2), a paired difference
of 2.9 points (95% CI 2.4 to 3.4). Both reviewers are the same model, so
they may share blind spots. The fixtures and review records are in the
Hugging Face dataset at revision ceaba90:
https://huggingface.co/datasets/xiaoyuanwang/ifbench-audit/tree/ceaba90ba6a2acac8fd8b51368a37e27c0ba688f.
The skill's reviewer prompt is adapted from the audit's.

Part of #10060.

[atlas] Add a Daytona-safe flag to RL data sources (#11196)

The curation inventory now records whether running a source fits the
Daytona
snapshot budget: at most ten unique snapshots. Sources without the
agentic
tag are safe automatically because they never provision a sandbox;
agentic
sources carry an authored `DaytonaSafety` verdict that stays
`unassessed`
until assessed. Atlas renders Safe, Unsafe, or a dash and sorts and
exports
the column like the others; the sources API serves
`DAYTONA_SAFE_SNAPSHOT_LIMIT` so the UI quotes the canonical budget. The
field rides the declaration JSONB through catalog publication and the
loader without schema changes.

All 133 agentic sources carry an assessed verdict: 108 safe, 25 unsafe.

- Converted TaskTrove sources run on digest-pinned agent images with
  worker-placed graders, so each needs one or two snapshots.
- Native TaskTrove releases publish per-source environment groups in
their
  pinned provenance. Sources with more than ten distinct environments
  (OpenSWE, R2E-Gym, SWE-Gym, MiMo code, cyber and general, native
  CalibForge, Harbor Hub skill2env, toolscale) are unsafe.
- Nemotron Ultra SWE-pivot components run per-instance SWE-Gym and
  SWE-rebench-V2 environments and are unsafe; their tool-use and
  judge-graded components are safe.
- The Smartie SWE-Smith campaign releases stage one image per parent
task

  share one environment and are safe.
- The converted repository sources build per-task Docker contexts: swe
rebench provisions 15 actor and 17691 grader builds, swesmith 5 actor
and
  12927 grader builds. Both are unsafe.

The flag counts unique snapshots, following the Daytona preflight
runbook.
Where a pinned release's own snapshot-safety verdict also weighs tag and
dependency mutability (MiMo music and webdev: one shared environment
each

commits.author: loom-oa-dev[bot]
commits.message:
[inference] Prepare Hugging Face weights before starting inference (#10277)

Prepare uncached Hugging Face checkpoints on CPU before reserving
serving accelerators. The coordinator checks the shared cache first when
its cluster and region can be proven to match serving; a complete
snapshot skips the prepare job. Cache misses and other placements use a
CPU job with the serving placement constraints. GPU children inside an
Iris job keep preparing without a cluster pin because child jobs stay on
their parent cluster. Root GPU submissions without a cluster pin skip
preparation with a warning. TPU placement without a cluster pin also
skips when regions are unrestricted, or unset at the root; one explicit
region or an inherited parent region keeps preparation enabled.

Preparation and serving use the same model resolver. The served model
and speculative draft each keep their own pinned commit across both
stages. Each prepare job gets one failure retry within a four-hour
preparation wait budget. Preparation timeouts fail pending evaluations
without entering the serving-startup retry loop.

An explicit CoreWeave `target_cluster` on the serving resources still
submits a CPU job when warm: the local controller reports its cluster as
`local`, which cannot prove a named match. Eval children leave that
field unset, inherit their orchestrator’s cluster, and can reuse a warm
cache in-process. A warm `Qwen/Qwen3-0.6B` probe on cw-rno2a
(`/karan/task380-warm-prepare-7777b7b37f`) took 64.7 s client-observed,
including a 4.8 s submit RPC. Controller timestamps show 25.0 s from
submission to code start (including about 1.7 s setup), 9.7 s for
imports and cache checks, and 18.3 s from code completion to terminal
status. The warm resolver itself took 0.12 s. This probe included a
federation hop from marin; a local CoreWeave orchestrator skips that
hop. No serving accelerators were reserved.

See the [evaluation
guide](https://github.com/marin-community/marin/blob/agent/20261019-fix-9233/docs/tutorials/run-lm-evals.md)
for cache-placement limits and hosted-judge preparation behavior, and
the
[design](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1-rRhP9mB4hpbzXwxUfPUTejwUVk1w68BOIs9TWdsBFk/edit)
for the broader pre-caching plan.

The latest affected run completed all 893 selected cases: 888 passed, 5
failed, 0 skipped, 0 xfailed, and 0 unfinished. The five task-driver
failures also reproduce on main because the local Python lacks
os.pidfd_open. An earlier full-branch run reached the 600 s session
limit with 19 cases unfinished; CI provides the full check.

Fixes #9233

commits.author: atqamar
commits.message:
[skyrl] Fix Softmax Collapse in trainer logprobs and entropy (#10682)

Confident tokens in the trainer keep a small negative log-probability, a
positive entropy and a gradient on the sampled token. Log-probabilities,
entropy and selected-token distillation log-probabilities are computed
in fp32 from logit margins, following [A Fix for Softmax and
Cross-Entropy](https://jonbarron.info/softmaxfix/): the vocabulary sum
leaves out the top logit, and `log1p` and `expm1` add it back. The paper
names the failure this avoids Softmax Collapse. With a token's margin
defined as its top logit minus the log-sum-exp of all other logits,
Transformer Engine's cross-entropy returns exactly 0 once the margin
exceeds about 16.6 in fp32, and entropy computed in bf16 returns 0 once
the margin is about 6.

One module, `skyrl_train/stable_softmax.py`, serves policy
log-probabilities, entropy and distillation. On CUDA at tensor
parallelism 1 it runs one Triton kernel; other layouts use the same
formulas in chunked PyTorch. The k3 estimate of KL divergence, `exp(r) -
1 - r` for log-ratio `r`, uses `expm1`.

Tests compare values and gradients with an 80-digit Decimal reference on
CPU, H100 and GB200, with the top logit placed in every kernel block, at
vocabularies 151,936 and 128,256. PR CI runs the CPU tests, and the
nightly Grug lane on H100 runs the kernel test.

| Measure | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Log-probability of a token whose margin is 20 or 30 (test rows, fp32)
| 0 | within 5e-6 relative of the reference |
| Entropy of a token whose margin is above about 6 (test rows, bf16
logits) | 0 | within 5e-6 relative of the reference |
| Saved Qwen2.5-0.5B batch: active tokens with entropy exactly 0 | 20.0%
| 0% |
| Same batch: mean entropy | 1.1274 nats | 1.1328 nats |
| Same batch, one PPO step: policy loss | 0.30847583 | 0.30847582 |
| Same batch, one PPO step: gradient norm | 28.773 | 28.779 |

The entropy metric changes at this commit, because main's bf16 entropy
reports 0 for confident tokens: on this batch it reads 0.5% higher.
Expect that change when comparing entropy curves from before and after
this commit.

H100, vocabulary 151,936, 32,768 tokens, median of ten repetitions;
memory is peak allocation above the inputs.

| Pass | Main | This PR |
|---|---|---|
| Training: log-probabilities with gradient, entropy without | 67.4 ms,
9.56 GiB | 29.6 ms, 9.27 GiB |
| Scoring: log-probabilities without gradient | 7.42 ms | 7.65 ms |
| Three training steps of the CatCount RL canary, seconds per step (two
runs each) | 8.54–8.63 | 8.11 |

Benchmark and replay programs:
[marin-logbooks](https://github.com/marin-community/marin-logbooks/tree/3d94c84d0ae9ba6925b37de671760dc01f4fa6e4/logbooks/10682-softmax-numerics).

With `trainer.algorithm.batch_invariant=true` at tensor parallelism 1,
the kernel computes each row independently. Where vLLM returns exactly 0
for a confident token, the trainer log-probability is slightly negative,
below 1.2e-7 in absolute value. An fp32 bit-mismatch count such as the
one in #10634 rises on those tokens.

commits.author: mcwitt
commits.message:
[skyrl] Apply Grug log scaling in the Megatron Grug model (#11129)

The current hero checkpoint uses log scaling: on global-attention
layers, each query is multiplied by `(1 + alpha * ln(max(n / n_floor,
1))) ** power` on top of the fixed `qk_mult`, where `n` is the number of
keys the query sees in its own document. With the hero's floor of
65,536, the factor is 1 up to that position and 1.296 at 262,144.
SkyRL's Megatron Grug model, the only model SFT and RL train the hero
with, applied only the fixed scale, so it would train the long-context
checkpoint at the wrong attention temperature.

`GrugMoeConfig` now reads `log_scaling_n_floor`, `log_scaling_alpha` and
`log_scaling_power` and accepts artifact schema 3 as split experts; null
fields apply no factor. The Megatron attention computes `n` per packed
document. Under context parallelism it maps each rank's two zigzag
chunks back to global document positions, matching the JAX model's
per-segment count. The eager HF model, which cannot apply the factor,
rejects a config with the fields set.

On 2 H100s, Megatron matched a tiny JAX Hero oracle with a 16-key floor
unpacked, packed and under CP2, with the fields set and null, to bf16
noise; it was closer to the right oracle than to ones with an off-by-one
key count or a 10% parameter error. The CPU tests check the visible-key
counts against Megatron's packing on every CP rank and the factor at the
Hero's settings exactly.

RL rollouts need a vLLM wheel with marin-community/vllm#121. SkyRL's
pinned wheel predates it and rejects schema 3, so RL on the log-scaled
Hero fails at load until the pin moves.

Part of #11127

commits.author: ClassicLarry
commits.message:
Belay: re-queue a planned idea a session escalated before launching (#10951)

A session can report an idea `planned` and then escalate before any run
launches. Idea #5's registry write failed after its first rung's plan
was posted, for example. Re-queue accepted only `approved` or `recorded`
ideas, and the admin page didn't show such an idea, so it could be
neither re-queued nor declined.

A planned idea now counts as stalled only with proof that nothing
launched:
- it was escalated;
- it has no Belay run under its registry id, ladder rungs included;
- it has been quiet for 20 minutes, two watcher passes, so a run
submitted just before the escalation would have been reported.

Re-queue and Decline accept such an idea and refuse any other planned
idea with the reason. The admin page lists planned escalations with the
other ideas that need a maintainer.

commits.message:
[iac] Let Belay runs read the tokenizer mirror and the compilation and autotune caches (#10955)

Every run the first Belay sessions launched failed at startup. The Belay
key (#10931) is refused reads of `marin-us-east-02a/marin/tokenizers/`,
where `levanter.tokenizers` stages `hero-bpe-v16384` through
`mirror://tokenizers/`; the Hugging Face fallback then 401s. The same
key is refused the shared JAX compilation cache
(`marin/compilation-cache/`) and the XLA autotune cache (`<temp
bucket>/tmp/ttl=30d/xla-per-fusion-autotune/`). Those two only cost cold
compiles.

This adds all three to the Belay user's read prefixes, both in the
`marin-belay` org policy grants and in the bucket-policy denies. The
caches stay read-only: a Belay run reuses compiled programs and autotune
results but can't write entries other runs would load, so its writes
there fail with a warning, as they do now. I scanned the failed runs'
logs; these were the only refused paths, but the runs died before data
loading and evals.

Apply with `pulumi up --target` on `policy-belay`,
`policy-marin-us-east-02a` and `policy-marin-us-east-08a`.

commits.author: mvanhorn
commits.message:
resolve Grug multislice smoke dataset pins to a region that has them (#11070)

## Background

The Grug multislice smoke dies while preparing datasets and never
submits its TPU training job. Nemotron tokenization, together with
StarCoder and ProofPile, exits because no training files match under the
us-east5 raw bucket, and the parent reports nine failed steps.

The training sets are pinned as paths relative to the region the canary
runs in. In us-east5 those copies are failed executor stubs, so the pins
are rebuilt by tokenizing, but the raw corpora are not in that region
and the rebuild finds no training files.

## Summary of the fix

Each pinned training cache is adopted from the first usable copy under
the local prefix and then the other GCS data buckets, and that copy is
streamed in place. A copy is usable only with a tokenizer record and
either a success status or a finished train ledger; failed,
dependency-failed, running, and stub-only copies are skipped, an
unreadable prefix is skipped, and no usable copy raises
FileNotFoundError. Paloma and uncheatable validation sets are removed,
leaving a training-only mixture.

## Verification

Ran `uv run pyrefly check` locally on macOS for the marin
multislice_smoke_resources change; it fails the same way on the base
branch, so the failure predates this change (it fails the same way on
upstream/main). A run with the marin multislice_smoke_resources change
reverted gave no clear result, so no test is shown to catch this bug.
The new test experiments/ferries/test_grug_multislice_smoke.py did not
run here: the test environment could not run it.

Fixes #11042

AI was used for assistance.
